texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: April’s background ▶
texts.text: April’s background ▶

texts.label: text
texts.orig: April didn’t study marketing but engineering at school and worked at a startup when they were still called “small companies.” She ended up working for a “loser product” in a marketing role that she helped reposition and that took off. Her boss quit, so she became the VP of Marketing, which made her discover positioning as a fundamental concept in marketing that actually didn’t have a methodology. She is, today, talking about this methodology in her book, specifically for B2B SAAS growth stage/scale-ups.
texts.text: April didn’t study marketing but engineering at school and worked at a startup when they were still called “small companies.” She ended up working for a “loser product” in a marketing role that she helped reposition and that took off. She is, today, talking about this methodology in her book, specifically for B2B SAAS growth stage/scale-ups.

texts.orig: Defining positioning, and when you know you have a positioning problem ▶
texts.text: Defining positioning, and when you know you have a positioning problem ▶

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Positioning as a concept is not new; it defines how your product is the best in the world at delivering some value that a well-defined set of companies care a lot about.
texts.text: Positioning as a concept is not new; it defines how your product is the best in the world at delivering some value that a well-defined set of companies care a lot about.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: It's hard to measure bad or weak positioning, but you can feel a sluggishness (e.g. the lightbulb does not come on with a customer unless they have an extra sales call). So how do you assess positioning?
texts.text: It's hard to measure bad or weak positioning, but you can feel a sluggishness (e.g. the lightbulb does not come on with a customer unless they have an extra sales call). So how do you assess positioning?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Hang out with Sales. You’ll get to listen to customers who are like, “Back up and pitch it to me again. Can you say that again?” Sometimes they’d say, “Oh, you are like Salesforce” or “I can do this on a spreadsheet; why do I need you?” And in this confusion lies your positioning problem.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Company misalignment vs. positioning issues ▶
texts.text: Company misalignment vs. positioning issues ▶

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Most cases April has dealt with are misalignment problems within the org and not positioning problems. The founder often has the positioning story done right with their early customer calls, but their C-level team “is not doing or getting it right.” Or the market conditions have changed (e.g. during Covid), where positioning needs a re-evaluation and Product or Marketing has to convince the founders.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: The essential five steps to figuring out your product’s positioning ▶
texts.text: The essential five steps to figuring out your product’s positioning ▶

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Competitive alternatives: What do we have to position against? It’s like saying, who do you have to beat in order to win a deal?
texts.text: Competitive alternatives: What do we have to position against? It’s like saying, who do you have to beat in order to win a deal?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: You often have a status quo alternative, like Zendesk, that is easy to ignore, but you shouldn’t because in B2B you lose about 40% of deals to “no decision,” which actually means you lost to the spreadsheet, you lost to pen and paper, you lost to interns. And if you’re not positioning well against that product, you’re never going to get the customer to come off that.

And if you’re not positioning well against that product, you’re never going to get the customer to come off that.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Key unique attributes: What makes you different? These are key product capabilities or feature functions that the alternatives don’t have.
texts.text: Key unique attributes: What makes you different? These are key product capabilities or feature functions that the alternatives don’t have.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Translate into value: The above unique attributes often bucket into themes of value that are differentiated.
texts.text: Translate into value: The above unique attributes often bucket into themes of value that are differentiated.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Customers who care are your target customers: What are the characteristics of a target account that make them really, really care a lot about that value?
texts.text: Customers who care are your target customers: What are the characteristics of a target account that make them really, really care a lot about that value?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Market you win: What’s the context I position this thing in that makes my value obvious to the people I’m going after?

texts.orig: The difference between positioning, messaging, and branding ▶
texts.text: The difference between positioning, messaging, and branding ▶

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: These concepts are distinct, because positioning is a fundamental precursor to messaging. By messaging, people mean “This is the text on the homepage.” You can’t write that until you understand the value for whom.
texts.text: These concepts are distinct, because positioning is a fundamental precursor to messaging. By messaging, people mean “This is the text on the homepage.” You can’t write that until you understand the value for whom.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: You can’t figure out what the “brand” stands for until you know the target buyer and the differentiation for the brand to be distinct.
texts.text: You can’t figure out what the “brand” stands for until you know the target buyer and the differentiation for the brand to be distinct.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: How should early-stage companies think about positioning? ▶
texts.text: How should early-stage companies think about positioning? ▶

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: The actual 5-step exercise above takes a week and depends on how contentious the existing alignment is.
texts.text: The actual 5-step exercise above takes a week and depends on how contentious the existing alignment is.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: For an early-stage company trying to find PMF, the positioning makes less sense, because there is a lot of validation of the product hypothesis first. Allow the market and customers to pull you as opposed to nailing positioning. For example, if you are selling fish nets—if your thesis is that it’s only for tuna, if it fails, it fails hard. In the beginning, you can just use it for all kinds of big fish and let’s see where it goes. Maybe it’s good for grouper, and this you figure out by being flexible.

In the beginning, you can just use it for all kinds of big fish and let’s see where it goes. Maybe it’s good for grouper, and this you figure out by being flexible.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: You feel the need for nailing positioning when you start seeing common patterns with the customers, e.g. they all have Zendesk, are 50-people strong, and are yet to hire their COO.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: What’s the difference between segmentation and personas? ▶
texts.text: What’s the difference between segmentation and personas? ▶

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: In B2B, you first segment your customers via firmographics, i.e. things like how many employees, revenue, geography, etc. Then, a more actionable segmentation is: “three-member or more creative agencies that follow a specific firmographic profile and have a budget of 20K and they use Notion.” Often in enterprise B2B decision-making, there are between five and seven people involved, so the tighter your segment, the more effective your marketing team is.
texts.text: In B2B, you first segment your customers via firmographics, i.e. things like how many employees, revenue, geography, etc. Then, a more actionable segmentation is: “three-member or more creative agencies that follow a specific firmographic profile and have a budget of 20K and they use Notion.” Often in enterprise B2B decision-making, there are between five and seven people involved, so the tighter your segment, the more effective your marketing team is.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: After segmentation, personas come to know who the internal champion of the prospective buyer is. For example, this could be John, who is the head of Sales Ops, and it’s his responsibility to build consensus and galvanize the deal, including their boss, who’s the actual check writer. John becomes the gatekeeper and the most important persona, and if your product is not differentiated, you don’t get on John’s shortlist.
